facts: $\mathrm{C}(f) = \Omega(\mathrm{UC}_{\min}(f)^{1.22})$ for an explicit family [BHT17].

$\mathrm{UC}(f) = \mathrm{SP}(f)$ exactly, for every $f$. Splitting a monochromatic subcube partition by colour gives an unambiguous family on each side, and conversely two unambiguous families glue into a partition. The two ids are kept apart only because the literature uses them in different places -- \(\mathrm{SP}(f)\) is what lifts to the communication partition number, $\mathrm{UC}$ is what appears in low-sensitivity constructions -- so $\mathrm{D}$ vs $\mathrm{SP}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ vs $\mathrm{UC}$ are one open problem, not two. The one-sided $\mathrm{UC}_{\min}$ has no such partner.
$\mathrm{D}(f) = O(\mathrm{UC}(f)^2)$; separations up to $\mathrm{D} = \tilde\Omega(\mathrm{UC}^2)$ come from the Göös-Pitassi-Watson function.

up.note: Take an optimal partition of $\mathrm{Dom}(f)$ into monochromatic subcubes of codimension at most $\mathrm{SP}(f)$ and split it by colour. Every subcube is monochromatic, so each one is a certificate; the $1$-subcubes cover $f^{-1}(1)$ disjointly and the $0$-subcubes cover $f^{-1}(0)$ disjointly, which is exactly unambiguity on each side. Hence $\mathrm{UC}^0, \mathrm{UC}^1 \le \mathrm{SP}$ and so $\mathrm{UC} \le \mathrm{SP}$. Nothing here asks the two colour classes to be individually minimal, which is why the argument goes through and $\mathrm{UC}(f) = \mathrm{SP}(f)$ for every $f$, total or partial. The zoo keeps the two ids separate because the literature does -- $\mathrm{SP}$ is the object that lifts to the partition number in communication complexity, $\mathrm{UC}$ the one that appears in low-sensitivity constructions -- but no function can separate them.

\(Unambiguous certificate complexity and subcube partition complexity are the *same* measure.\) partial Settled #

Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\mathrm{UC}(f) \le \mathrm{SP}(f)\)
    Take an optimal partition of $\mathrm{Dom}(f)$ into monochromatic subcubes of codimension at most $\mathrm{SP}(f)$ and split it by colour. Every subcube is monochromatic, so each one is a certificate; the $1$-subcubes cover $f^{-1}(1)$ disjointly and the $0$-subcubes cover $f^{-1}(0)$ disjointly, which is exactly unambiguity on each side. Hence $\mathrm{UC}^0, \mathrm{UC}^1 \le \mathrm{SP}$ and so $\mathrm{UC} \le \mathrm{SP}$. Nothing here asks the two colour classes to be individually minimal, which is why the argument goes through and $\mathrm{UC}(f) = \mathrm{SP}(f)$ for every $f$, total or partial. The zoo keeps the two ids separate because the literature does -- $\mathrm{SP}$ is the object that lifts to the partition number in communication complexity, $\mathrm{UC}$ the one that appears in low-sensitivity constructions -- but no function can separate them.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{UC}(\oplus_n) = \mathrm{SP}(\oplus_n) = n\)
    witness: \(\oplus_n\)

The consequence worth remembering is that $\mathrm{D}$ vs $\mathrm{SP}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ vs $\mathrm{UC}$ are literally the same open problem, and the one-sided $\mathrm{UC}_{\min}$ -- which is not an equality with anything partition-flavoured -- is where the interesting behaviour lives.

see also: \(\mathrm{UC}(f)\), \(\mathrm{SP}(f)\), \(\mathrm{UC}_{\min}(f)\), \(\mathrm{C}(f)\), \(\mathrm{D}(f)\) data/relations/01-classical-core.yaml

A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing

constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
